newsitem.title: USA: News groups want Oklahoma blast documents unsealed.
newsitem.headline: News groups want Oklahoma blast documents unsealed.

text.p: A coalition of 33 news organisations Thursday urged an appeals court to unseal dozens of key documents in the Oklahoma City bombing case.

"The documents were sealed (by the trial judge) in violation of the public's constitutional and common law rights of access," the wire services, networks, newspapers and broadcast stations argued to the U.S. 10th Circuit Court of Appeals.

The documents include Federal Bureau of Investigation reports and defence documents submitted to the judge for the trials of Timothy McVeigh and Terry Nichols, former Army buddies accused of last year's bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building. The truck bomb killed 168 people.

The news organisations, including Reuters, argued U.S. District Judge Richard Matsch ignored Supreme Court decisions that purportedly required him to consider other means to ensure a fair trial before resorting to sealing documents.

Separately, Matsch conducted a rare unannounced closed court session Thursday in which he ordered prosecutors to turn over classified government information to McVeigh's attorneys, McVeigh's lead attorney said. The content of the information is sealed.
The two defendants, who face the death penalty if convicted, will be tried separately with McVeigh's trial held first starting March 31.
The case was moved to Denver to insure a fairer trial than the defendants could have received in Oklahoma, the court ruled.
